concerns.text: Task T031 mandates a 'Paired Statistical Test' (t-test/Wilcoxon) as the PRIMARY analysis. This directly violates FR-005 and SC-001 which require a paired t-test, BUT contradicts the Plan's 'Critical Methodological Note' which explicitly REJECTS the t-test due to zero-variance in the theoretical human baseline, mandating 'Distribution Overlap Analysis' instead. The task implements a method the plan explicitly forbids as primary, creating a fatal semantic conflict between the spec's requirement and the plan's approved methodology.

Task T024 defines stability assessment based on the consistency of 't-test/Wilcoxon' conclusions. This violates FR-009 which requires assessing the stability of the 'comparison' (the primary method). Since the Plan (Methodological Approach) replaces the t-test with 'Distribution Overlap Analysis' as the primary method, T024's reliance on t-test stability is a semantic weakening of the requirement to validate the actual chosen methodology.

Task T032 instructs to 'Reuse... statistical_analysis.py... to perform Shapiro-Wilk, Paired Statistical Test, and Sensitivity Analysis'. This forces the implementation of the 'Paired Statistical Test' (t-test) which the Plan explicitly states is 'mathematically inappropriate' and replaced by 'Distribution Overlap Analysis'. The task fails to preserve the Plan's constitutional constraint regarding the statistical method for the theoretical baseline.

Task T036 requires the report to include 'selected analysis name (Paired t-test or Wilcoxon)'. This contradicts the Plan's 'Methodological Approach' which mandates the report include 'Test Name (Overlap/T-Test)' where Overlap is primary. By forcing the t-test name as the primary identifier, the task weakens the Plan's requirement to highlight the Distribution Overlap Analysis as the valid method for zero-variance baselines.
